input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: HERENT. Summary: Digital Reporting and Live Broadcast of City Council, Social Welfare Council and Committees. Description: The object of this assignment is the complete processing and access of the digital audio reports of the councils and committees of the municipality of Herent, including: • processing and hosting of audio reports; • automatic or manual subtitling of the audio reports; • making the audio reports available via a web portal, integrated into or visually aligned with the website of the municipality of Herent; • live audio streaming of all meetings of the municipal council, OCMW council and committees (basic requirement); • transcription of the audio report (via a user-friendly and easy-to-organize application, for example AI-based transcription); • searchability of the reports by agenda item, speaker and time code; • archiving of all sessions in a clear, calendar-based manner as an alternative to the disappearing Notubiz calendar function. The purpose of this assignment is to increase the transparency of the policy process, increase the involvement of residents and the threshold to follow both live and afterwards meetings. Summary: Production of Labour Market Policy (Lmp) Statistics and Maintenance of the Eu Labour Market Policy Statistical Database. Description: The “labour market policy (LMP) statistics” project is a data collection developed by the European Commission to monitor the implementation and development of targeted employment policies across the EU. LMP statistics have been used to monitor both active and passive interventions in the labour market and, in particular, relevant areas of the EU employment guidelines. The LMP database contains more than 20 000 interventions reported by EU Member States and Norway since 1997, specifically data on expenditure and participants broken down by various dimensions. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: ASSOCIATION OF ISSUING BODIES. Summary: Framework Agreement for an it Application Officer. Description: The framework contract is intended to appoint an independent freelance IT application officer that will carry out the contract in close cooperation with the AIB secretariat staff, more specific the AIB secretary general and the AIB IT contract manager and is available on average 4-5 days per week during the duration of the contract. The AIB secretariat is based in Brussels and has a staff of an average of 4 FTE, both employees and contractors. The deployment of the IT application officer is flexible depending on the necessity. The intended duration of the contract is 4 years. Reciprocal termination clauses will be provided in the procurement documents. Remote work (also from outside of Belgium, within the EU, EFTA or Energy Community) is possible. However, since the AIB secretariat and staff are based in Brussels, occasional presence in Brussels is required in alignment with the secretary general (travel costs covered by AIB). Please note: the contract will stipulate a maximum hourly fee of the application officer. At the time of publication of this selection guide, the maximum fee has not yet been defined. However, the maximum fee as defined in the contract will not exceed 90 EUR/hour, excl. VAT. By submitting a request to participate, the candidate agrees to the terms of a maximum fee which will be defined in the contract. <br> Doc Title: Framework agreement for an IT Application officer <br> Contract Type: services. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN FREE TRADE ORGANISATION, FINANCIAL MECHANISM OFFICE. Summary: Fund Operator for the Social Dialogue and Decent Work Programme under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2021-2028. Description: Through the Norway Grants, Norway works closely with partners in 13 EU Member States in Central and Southern Europe and the Baltic States, to contribute to the reduction of social and economic disparities in the European Economic Area (EEA) and the strengthening of bilateral cooperation. Support to social dialogue and decent work has been a key priority for the Norway Grants since 2004. The Agreement between Norway and the European Union on the Norwegian Financial Mechanism (2021-2028) sets aside €14,640,000 for a fund for social dialogue and decent work. The Social Dialogue and Decent Work Fund (SDDW Fund) is made available to actors in all the Norway Grants Beneficiary States, to strengthen social dialogue between workers- organisations, employers- organisations and public authorities and promote decent work. The Financial Mechanism Office (FMO) is the Brussels-based secretariat for the Norway Grants. The FMO is affiliated to the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), and reports to the Foreign Ministry of Norway. The decision-making body of the Norway Grants is the Foreign Ministry of Norway. The FMO has been entrusted with the role of Programme Operator (PO) of the SDDW Fund. The role of the PO is to select and contract the Fund Operator, monitor compliance with the legal framework of the SDDW Fund and follow up on the progress and quality of fund implementation. Explanation: The Hoegaarden municipal council is reviewing the current software landscape surrounding its civil affairs and reception department (population, civil registry and immigration affairs). Currently the service worked in different applications from different suppliers. This has a number of limitations: • files are becoming more complex and family members are increasingly registered in different registers and have different questions at the same time (such as an application for permanent residence in Belgium, simultaneously with an application for Belgian nationality); • employees who take on different roles within the cell must regularly switch to a different working environment; • the learning curve for new employees is unnecessarily high because they have to get to know multiple applications; • a more flexible work organization within the service is more difficult to achieve; • cost-effectiveness, including in terms of connections to be made. Therefore wishes the board to receive one total quotation for the following modules: • Population, including digital housing control; • Foreigners; • Civil status. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: FLEMISH ENVIRONMENT AGENCY. Summary: Preparation of Regional Groundwater Models of the Phreatic Aquifer for the Groundwater Simulator. Description: The object of the assignment concerns the preparation of regional groundwater models of the phreatic aquifer for the groundwater simulator. With the groundwater simulator (see https://www.dov.vlaanderen.be/page/grondwatersimulator) the effect of local interventions in the phreatic groundwater can be calculated everywhere in Flanders. For this purpose, the groundwater simulator uses five regional Modflow6 groundwater flow models in the background. The aim of this assignment is to improve the regional to improve groundwater flow models (Modflow6) used in the groundwater simulator. There are currently 5 regional models in the background of the groundwater simulator. The remodeling of the regional models aims to: to refine grid sizes and obtain a finer layer layout. Some of the existing models will therefore be split into smaller areas. Furthermore, a thorough calibration must be carried out with attention to a passing grade differentiation within the Quaternary Aquifer. Any new available data sets must be processed. The present assignment concerns 6 model areas that have been bundled into 3 plots. Each lot contains two models Category (CPV code): Analytical, scientific, mathematical or forecasting software development services (72212460). Published Date: 2025-10-26. Closing Date: 2025-11-20. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: BRUSSELS CONNECTIT. Summary: Analysis and Advice Financial Planning and Forecasting. Description: Within the SPRB, the current multi -year budget and staff planning process is fragmented and non -standardized. Each administration uses its own working tools and methods. The data is exported to Excel files, adapted to the expected structure and loaded in different tools, which creates confusion as to the source of forecasts and simulations. This mission aims to examine how to develop a uniform working method and what tools would be appropriate for this purpose. The study focuses on three cases of representatives involving four administrations: Brussels Synergie, Finance and Budget, Local Powers and Connect IT. The results of this study will lead to a recommendation concerning L-Organization to be implemented, the knowledge necessary to acquire as well as the support tools, which will be implemented in a later phase. Description: The SNCB has a network of 300 to 350 installations for digital signage/narrowcasting spread over more than 100 sites in Belgium. This solution, B-Vision, is an essential tool for the SNCB in order to inform its employees in the field (train guides, train drivers, staff in stations and workshops, etc.). The content distributed on the screens consists in part of corporate content and partly of local/operational content. Several hundred content creators from all directions of the SNCB, can publish content with different Rights levels: Some may publish content on a single screen, others on a game (for example, all screens of train drivers) or on the entire network. The content is targeted in the level of an individual installation (for example, specific information for Employees of a specific train driving, train control, etc.). Twee extra behoeften worden toegevoegd. Het gaat om de constructie van een digital twin en een netsimulator voor oefeningen en opleidingen. Deze functies zijn gelinkt aan de vorige, in die zin dat ze op hetzelfde netmodel en dezelfde berekeningswijze steunen. Van de respondenten wordt verwacht dat ze voor elke behoefte beschrijven waarover ze reeds beschikken en welke grote of kleine verschillen er zijn ten opzichte van deze beschrijving. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: REGIONAAL TECHNOLOGISCH CENTRUM ANTWERPEN. Summary: Crm Rtc Antwerpen. Description: RTC Antwerp currently has six employees, each responsible for specific areas of expertise. Based on these areas, they build their own networks and maintain contacts independently. Contact details are currently kept individually, often in Excel, Outlook, or other personal files. RTC Antwerp has a clear and functional website. Most contact data is collected via registration or request forms on the website. However, there is a strong internal need to manage this data in a structured and centralized way. In addition, RTC Antwerp observes that a lot of data circulates within the organization, often in a fragmented manner. Data must regularly be processed, copied, or manually counted multiple times—for instance, for reporting to authorities or subsidy providers, creating thematic contact lists, or sending newsletters. As a result, there is a growing need for a streamlined and efficient approach to managing contacts, registrations, material loans, and other data flows. RTC Antwerp is therefore seeking a stable and high-performing CRM system that is compatible with the existing website and capable of structurally supporting these needs. Project Goals Internal Processes RTC Antwerp aims to improve internal efficiency by automating workflows and centralizing information related to planning, events, and contacts. The goal is to significantly reduce the time currently spent on repetitive administrative tasks, creating more room for what truly matters: sustainable relationship management .... Published Date: 2025-07-01. Closing Date: 2025-08-01. Competition: ICB. Financier Name: Self Financed

input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: AZ OOSTENDE. Summary: Service Management Software Tool. Description: The General Hospital Oostende wishes to proceed to the acquisition of an advanced, user -friendly and future -oriented Service Management Software (SMS) tool. The PSO will provide quality assurance for all the deliverables produced by the contractors, and offer strategic and technical advice to assist the Contracting Authority.
